routes.name: Professional card (residence for a self-employed person)

note: Belgium, read on the Immigration Office's own pages (dofi.ibz.be, read 2026-10-30): the contribution fee (amounts as of 1 January 2026), the single permit, the professional card and EU citizens' right of entry and residence. A foreigner working for a Belgian employer over 90 days holds a single permit, applied for by the employer at the competent Region (the worker's principal place of work), decided jointly with the Immigration Office within a 4-month deadline, potentially extended; it is for that employment (work for the sponsor). The residence contribution is €152; the Region's own fees are apart and were not read. A self-employed artist needs the Region's professional card and a residence authorisation, asked by visa D at a Belgian post (contribution €242); the game reads the card as letting the holder take any engagement as self-employed. Citizens of the EU and of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland stay over 3 months as employees, self-employed, job seekers or with sufficient means, applying to their municipality for a registration certificate (Annex 19). The permits' terms, the long-term resident status (its page names only its Directive) and nationality's years are not on these pages and were not read, so no term, permanent route or count is kept.

sources.title: Single Permit, Immigration Office (read 2026-10-30)
sources.said: any citizen from a non-European country who wants to stay and work more than 90 days in Belgium must be a single permit holder. The employer must apply to the competent Region ... If the Region and the Immigration Office do not make any unfavourable decision within the 4-month deadline, potentially extended, the residence and work authorisations will be considered as being granted.

sources.said: one of the associated States of the European Union (Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland) ... An EU citizen has the right to stay in Belgium for more than 3 months if he/she meets one of the following conditions: He/she is an employee or a self-employed person in Belgium; ...
